_comment: Who is in the Eunoia ecosystem, and on what footing. Read by
scripts/global_audit, which resolves each `repo` through scripts/repos.local
the way the other scripts do, and by nothing else.
This is a list somebody maintains, not one anything derives: a footing is a
decision rather than a fact about a tree. `status` is the whole of what this
file asserts --
member      declares membership in its README, the check passes, and it
shares the approach docs/vision.md argues for. The second half
is a judgement and is not checked -- see below
associate   we have read it and it is load-bearing for us, and it is held
to none of this. Its README carries the affiliating note, which
names the ecosystem and says it is not held to the policy;
`vetted` is when a person last read it and meant this
candidate   the policy is addressed to it and it has not joined. No
vetting, no claim, and no obligation on anybody
foundation  the arrangement is downstream of it. We place no constraint on
it, we ask it for nothing, and we say what it is to us. The
entry is a fact about *our* arrangement and never a status
conferred on theirs -- see docs/policy.md
child       a child project inside another repository here. `parent`
names whose tree, `path` where in it, and `branch` the
branch of the parent its current work is on, where that is
not the default one. A child is never a checkout of its own,
and is listed by scripts/install_eo all the same: it is work
that exists and may be worth reading, and saying where it
lives costs a line. A name with no work behind it is a
different thing and is not here at all -- tools/ynoia/
names.md is the register of those
These are not a ladder. A member trades compliance for nothing; an associate
trades nothing for a claim we make about them. Moving between the two is not
a promotion in either direction, and reading the list as a ranking is the
mistake docs/policy.md is written to prevent.
`status` now carries one mechanical fact and, for a member, one judgement.
Only the mechanical half is ever read by a program: ecosystem.py --check
--online decides *declares / does not declare* for a member and a candidate,
and *carries the affiliating note / does not* for an associate. Whether a
member shares the approach is a vision question, nobody has the authority to
settle it, and no check here may ever acquire an opinion about it.
What is not in this list, deliberately: everything these tools are built
*with* rather than built *around*. Lean and its toolchain, the C++ ethos is
compiled by, Python, the CI runner. Several are more load-bearing than half
the rows here and none of them is a footing -- the line is subject matter,
not how much we rely on it, and this file lists tools built around the
calculus plus the one project all of it is downstream of. What those
dependencies cost is a different question, and it belongs to the auditor
described in tools/ynoia/requests.md rather than here.
A status is changed by a person. scripts/global_audit may report that one
looks wrong; it does not edit this file on its own.

anoieu.what: the analyzer and the fuzzer; keeps the ecosystem's policy

cvc5.what: the solver, and the owner of CPC. The ecosystem exists to serve it, and asks it for nothing

ethos.what: the proof checker, the home of the Eunoia manual, and the tree the ethos-eoc child project is in
ethos.why: every other reading of the language is measured against its behaviour, and this repository's oracle is a recording of it

ethos-eoc.what: the Eunoia compiler, and the semantics sets it ships

logos.what: the Lean development, and the owner of Cpc.eos
logos.why: the ecosystem's trust argument terminates here: nothing else states that the rules cvc5 emits are sound

eudaimonia.what: the calculus template: bring a signature, get a checker and its proofs

dokimasia.what: reads cvc5's proof-production C++ and asks what no proof step covers

koine.what: the shared machinery of the reporting loop: one implementation of the protocol rather than one per member

sapheneia.what: Eunoia described as a language definition rather than as a checker's manual

ynoia.what: whether the ecosystem's arrangement earns its machinery, and what it is missing

euthyna.what: what the proof in logos is made of, and where its weight sits

workflow-launcher.what: the first hour of a new tool's life, and a register of what this ecosystem's practice has turned out to be doing
